recipes.name: Sweet and Spicy Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Place sweet potatoes into a large mixing bowl; drizzle with olive oil. Season with paprika, brown sugar, black pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, poultry seasoning, chili powder, and cayenne pepper; toss until potatoes are evenly coated. Spread onto a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes, then turn potatoes over with a spatula. Continue baking until potatoes are golden and tender, 10 to 15 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet and Spicy Sweet Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This sweet potato seasoning made with paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, chili powder, and brown sugar adds fantastic flavor to roasted potatoes.

review.reviewBody: Yum!! I was attracted by the rave reviews by males (husbands, fiances) :) My husband likes spice and it wasn't too sweet for him like other sweet potatoe dishes. I took the suggestions to add a teaspoon of Cinnamon and a tablespoon of Brown Sugar. I only used 1 teaspoon of Paprika rather than 1 1/2 Tablespoons (?) and also left out the poultry seasoning. I used Olive Oil, adding only enough to cover the amount of potatoes I had so not quite 3T. I also oiled the glass dish I cooked them in so altogether, there was plenty of oil to not burn to the dish yet not too much. I look forward to making this again and using some of the other tips to create different flavors, like using fajita seasoning or steak seasoning instead of poultry seasoning. This recipe has opened my mind to the options of flavors (not to mention healthier dishes)for Sweet Potatoes, other than the typical super sweet, marshmallows, maple syrup, etc.

I've made this recipe about 5-6 times - usually the same ingredients, but different prep. If you toss the potato cubes in olive oil; toss again in the spices (I do all of this in a large ziploc bag); spread on parchment paper lined cookie sheet and roast. I find that this distributes the spice evenly and allows for a crispy finish - otherwise I tend to get big clumps of spices randomly on the potatoes, which is not as good. I also use a reduced amount of garlic salt instead of garlic powder and cut back on the cayenne a bit. Good with pork tenderloin or roast turkey - Yum!
This vegan favorite pot-luck dish has been my go-to for years. I add 1/4 cup orange juice before baking for a yummy sweet kick. Take copies of the recipe with you as you will be asked for it!

Pretty good. I wasn't sure whether the amount of paprika was a typo or not (does anyone know?), so I only added about a teaspoon of it. I followed the rest of the recipe and also added a couple of Tablespoons of dry sherry along with chopped onions and garlic (instead of powder because I didn't have any). I added some dried thyme, but didn't have any poultry seasoning. I let the whole mixture sit a mixing bowl until I was ready to put it in the oven (I like to get everything ready at once if I can earlier on in the day so dinner-time isn't as hectic). Took it out while the oven was preheating, then baked at 425 for 20 mins, flipped potatoes, and baked for another 20 mins. Came out really good, just not as sweet or as spicy as I'd expected. Next time I will use a Tablespoon of brown sugar as other reviewers did, and add a little more cayenne and chili powder (I did use hot chili powder).

This is a great seasoning for sweet potatoes! I used 1 Tbsp of brown sugar, 1 teaspoon of paprika and omitted the cayenne pepper but used the remaining ingredients as written. I did lightly sprinkle with sea salt right before serving. It turned out wonderful and even my husband, who is a plain meat and potatoes guy, loved it. I served it with baked chicken but this would be good with steak too. This will be my new go-to for sweet potatoes.

I am not a sweet potato lover, but loved this dish. I added 1 tsp of cinnamon, but kept the rest of the ingredients the same, put all ingredients except potatoes in plastic bag and mixed together, added potatoes and shook until well coated and emptied on to cookie sheet. We cut our chunks quite small and it did not take 40 min. to get them done. Keep an eye on them--you do not want to overdo them.

This has been my go-to sweet potato recipe for years now, so I'm finally reviewing it! I've done it several times roasting(always a classic), but I also used the spice blend the other day on sweet potatoes which I pressure-cooked and then blended in the food processor with the spice mix and a dollop of sour cream. These are like my ultimate comfort food. I've made it exactly as written, until I attempted the pressure cooker route with the spices the other day, and I love it. My only critique, for my own tastes, is that I always forget it's not really "spicy" at all as written. The amount of cayenne doesn't do it for me. But that's a personal preference and I love it all the same.

LOVED these sweet potatoes!!! I actually just cut the sweet potatoes into round slices probably 3 or 4 millimeters wide. In the mixture, the changes I included were:
 3 Tbls of brown sugar
 Instead of poultry seasoning, I used a little cajun and all purpose
 1 Tsp of cinnamon.
I baked at 425 degrees for closer to 35 minutes. WONDERFUL!

i got great reviews for Thanksgiving. I parboiled chunked Sweet potatoes (peeled) did the brown sugar with the spices. Instead of Cayenne i used sprinking of Cajun seasoning. Baked at recommended Temp but increased to 475 last 10 min to brown and make a little chewier outer layer. Thats it! very easy.

Man, this was good! My husband and I ate a whole pan for dinner one night lol. I didn't add the brown sugar because the sweet potatoes don't need added sugar; and I didn't use poultry seasoning because I don't buy it. To save a step, I put the diced sweet potatoes directly on the baking sheet, sprinkled them with oil and tossed them, then added the spice mixture and tossed again. No need to get an extra bowl dirty. These spicy sweet potatoes are so delicious, and so easy! Will be making this again and again! Thank you for the recipe!

These weren’t bad but they weren’t quite as sweet or spicy as I had hoped for. I upped the cayenne to 1/4 tsp. and used 3 tsp. of brown sugar. Even with the adjustments I still wish they had been sweeter. Also, I don’t think they need to cook quite as long. 10 minutes per side should prevent the sauce from burning onto the potatoes as well. I may try this again with some big adjustments.
Very easy to make and tastes fantastic!! I also add chunks of red onion and sometimes bacon bits!

First, it’s a recipe you can work with. I wouldn’t recommend doing it as is. I did that the first time I made them, they were over cooked and over spiced. Lower the oven temperature or reduce the cooking time. DO NOT use the amt of paprika it calls for- the first time I made them I did and - OH BOY! Waaaaay too much. The poultry seasoning is unnecessary. Either a little more brown sugar OR Mikes hot honey which allowed me to eliminate the Cayenne and chili powder.

I used smoked paprika....wouldn't recommend that in lieu of unless, because it was so smoky I mixed three tablespoons of maple syrup onto it and then salt.....Holy smokes..... (no pun intended) they were devoured.....Definitely a keeper.
it is realy good

This is a fairly simple recipe to put together and make. I ended up using the spice mixture with regular potatoes, as I did not have sweet potatoes on hand. The topping does adhere well to the potatoes with the aid of the olive oil. However, I personally found it a bit too spicy for my liking. If I were to try to make this again, I'd cut down on the cayenne and chili powder, and perhaps the paprika as well, so the brown sugar can shine through more.

Made this recipe for Thanksgiving this year instead of my usual sweet potato casserole and it was a very good change to our menu!! Everyone loved the little kick of flavor the cayenne gave it, while not being too spicy. Made it as stated but did double as we had a large crowd. Will make these again for just some everyday meals.
Love spice so added more chili and cayenne. Great balance in flavor! Household loved it.
My husband and I absolutely love this! Shared it with several others who have tried it, and they love it as well. You can substitute honey for the brown sugar - also nice!

We really enjoyed this seasoning mixture for the roasted sweet potatoes. I followed the recipe with the following exceptions...I intended to leave out the brown sugar all together but tasted a potato part way through cooking and ended up sprinkling 2 pinches and it was the perfect amount for us as we don't like our sweet potatoes sweetened too much. I used a little less paprika and doubled the cayenne pepper, personal preference. I had to use a different seasoning blend because my husband used the last of the chicken seasoning and didn't put it on the shopping list. 🤐 And I sprinkled 2 pinches of sea salt over the top before serving. My husband and one daughter gobbled them up. The other daughter who says she HATES sweet potatoes ate one potato and said "Not bad, doesn't make me gag" which is high praise coming from her. LOL. I will definitely make this again.
